Well.. its a game

As someone who's played a lot of zombie games on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ computer, and as someone who's played a lot of left 4 dead 2, well.. it's not really comparable. 

On one hand - its creative. The enemies are a mix of inspired from L4D and original ideas. Although, I don't really see why Flashers exist... they're easy to kill and their only purpose is to run around with a bright light. Other than the enemies, the visuals aren't any less than stunning. I love the environment the game gives us, and the story is decent at best. I also love the funky OST, too.

And the other hand - its bad. You'd find the gameplay a bit... floaty, if you know what I mean. The movement is meh, the gunplay is honestly terrible, and the cutscenes are all rushed with bad animations. The story is also a bit wonky, and the voice acting is AWFUL.

This game is a good concept, just executed terribly, but it can still be fun.

Once again, I've been bamboozled by the "from the makers of l4d" ads. I tried to find some entertainment value there for 6 hours, I really did, but all I was left with was the sadness of a missed refund opportunity.

It's sad, it's dead, and it smells like cheap plastic. Might still be fun enough for a run with a friend or two, but otherwise avoid.

Do not buy it, this game is irrevocably abysmal, 0/10. 

I played early access, complained loudly about its quality, put it down, and returned to have a go-over in 1.0, and it hasn’t improved. I’m going to draw comparisons to other horde shooters to demonstrate just how vacant of care this game is, notably; Left 4 Dead 2, Back 4 Blood, WWZ: Aftermath, Deep Rock Galactic, Helldivers 2, Payday 2, Killing Floor 2 and Warhammer 40K Darktide. If you are considering purchasing The Anacrusis, buy any of those games instead. 

[b]This game fails as a co-op shooter[/b] and disregards the foundational rule of the genre, clearly outlined objectives. It’s common to feel lost, get turned around in symmetrical spaces, scour the area for clues to where to go, and waste your precious health, ammo and time to the terrain. I have never encountered this kind of problem in any other shooter of this kind, and am frankly shocked that ‘being lost’ is supposed to be a feature. For reference, the ship of the Anacrusis is a pristine space-faring vessel overrun with a hostile alien force, and yet, there are no indications of other survivors than yourselves, no gore-splatter, no signage, no unpossessed corpses, no hi-vis paint, no HUD element, [i]and it feels like there is nothing to guide you to the next airlock or objective.[/i] It boggles the mind that an ‘all players required’ check is not indicated by floating markers, or has a loud tutorial message, or brazen contrast from the area around it. It’s not obvious, it will waste your time, if you play solo you’ll need to herd bots into it, and it constantly makes the game intolerable. Being dependent on tutorial messages is no substitute for good level design. 

[b]Horrible technical performance:[/b] [i]I have a RTX 4090, I expect a minimum 60fps and this game couldn’t do 20 during combat. Completely unacceptable.[/i] Constant stuttering and lighting strobes are common occurrences. Flashers, spawning hordes and incendiary grenades, heck - every grenade make the game unplayable. Even standard traversal through normal-looking areas with minimal combat tank frames consistently, and nothing fixes it. 

[b]Enemy design in the Anacrusis is bad on a foundational level.[/b] It is difficult to determine when common are dead unless you headshot because; there is no dismemberment system, minimal gore, the lack of glow of a common being dead is only on the front of the face, and no ragdolling. Common infected move in silence, yet hitting you only shows a small damage indicator, not aim-punch or hit sound. They have no personality, no overarching objective, dress similarly to other players, and lack characterisation to drive a player to slaughter them in their thousands. 
	Special infected are bland, horrible in gameplay, have no clearly defined weak spot in the model, and no audio queues. A ranged-grabbing enemy with no tell, a charging enemy without a counter, a spawning enemy which enters combat miles away and hides in corners? And no special enemy that targets players who wander off the main path(I wonder why)? All these scream underbaked, because with more player feedback, they individually wouldn’t be horrible. Even Back 4 Blood, a game that blatantly spawns multiple special infected behind players, has audio queues. I rest my case. 

[b]User Interface,[/b] if the game is going to have an infinite horde event, it needs to broadcast it clearly to the player multiple times and have an indicator that one is in progress. Even a “Current Objective: Survive”, or a recursive horde scream, or a massive banner indicator is better than nothing, and the Anacrusis has no downtime during waves, unlike Payday’s “Anticipation, Build, Sustain, Fade, Regroup” system. This leads to events in singleplayer where seemingly endless common spew from the corridor ahead, and you are stuck killing, unable to progress the objective. This attrition is fatiguing and discourages pushing forward, it’s negative nuance.
	Speaking of being tired, there is no replayability and no progression, there is nothing that you can bring into a level that alters player expression. There is no skill tree to grind out, no perk decks, or weapon upgrades. Since there is nothing more that I wish to do in the game, I’ll choose to uninstall it as fast as possible. 

In closing, it's all the trappings of modern gaming wrapped into a single painful package. It’s got the graphics of Unreal Engine 4 and skins like Fortnite, yet has worse gameplay than L4D, which came out over 16 years ago. I get it, Stray Bombay is a small indie company, but going 1.0 with a product this incomplete is Redfall levels of bad full release. The only saving grace is that the developers seem committed to this title, so expect in a few years that my review is invalidated by updates.

The Good: 
- The Atmosphere is good and the 1960s-style spaceship + characters are well thought out + designed. 
-  Fluent main menu. It's not too hard to navigate, and you get to pick your character from the menu and hop in-game immediately. 
- The Commons are just commons, they run at you and attack you just like l4d. and they wander around when not hostile / attracted to you're presence.
- Interesting Special Aliens, many are just L4D special infected but with new mechanics.
- When you enter a safe house, it plays a quick little "you survived!" cut scene with music before hopping back into gameplay. 
- Cool cutscene for the first finale when you pick up the data card, 
- Funny ending for after the finale, more lighthearted and cheery to say something like "You Made it!" 
- The community is not toxic at all, rather it's welcoming, which is a good start.
- This game is still being updated and has a roadmap for it. which is good, as this game should have it's potential executed.

The Bad: 
- Unclear directions during the first finale, the bombardment of commons made it hard for me to see what I had to do/go while the horde continued even after waiting out the data card. One of the AI had to say what I had to pick it up the 2nd time I played through.
- Bots won't shut up about using your pulse, yes I get it, it's a shove mechanic but more sci-fi-like, but they keep yelling at me like I'm not using it.
- Revive time is way slower than L4D. and during it, you're character just kneels there while the revive bar moves, no animation of them getting up or anything.
- It does not show stats after every safe room, rather it shows them all combined in the end, which I don't mind but I wanna know how much I killed during THAT level.
- Glitchy rag-dolls becoming stiff, it doesn't happen all the time, but the models freeze. should be fixed in later updates.
- No FSR, just DLSS. I like to use FSR for performance, but I hope they add it in the future.

This game is just L4D but in space, it's not a reskin or DLC for the game but it's own separate identity.

- As soon as you get to the main menu your chosen character stares deeply into your soul
- Poor audio mixing (companions screaming right into your ear no matter how far away you are from them, and quiet enemies)
- Companions never shutting up about telling you to use your shift ability
- Really dated and barebones graphics
- Linear, copy pasted, reused level design
- A short 3-4hr campaign with no actual story or cutscenes outside of minor dialogue
- Devs attacking players over asking about poor playercounts for the game
- No bosses, and the same few enemy types are reused the whole game
- No hit feedback on enemies
- Only 5 chapters with each consecutive chapter having fewer and shorter episodes
- No competitive co-op stats at the end of each episode or chapter like L4D2 (Could've sworn early access at least had this)
+ You can spam spawn weapons in the spawn room lagging the f out of that room
+ Workshop is cool and seems to have quite a few interesting fan additions
+ Nice costumes and skins to unlock just by playing, but how they unlock remains a mystery to me

Overall just a 2/10 go play WWZ and B4B instead if you want a good L4D like
I recommend this game :D It's a fun game :D Campaign 9.5/10 // Versus 10/10

This game is charming and easy to pick up/put down/come back to. The versus adds a lot of replayability and is done a lot better than most of its competitors. I also like Chet's videos explaining his decisions/logic, it gives me a deeper appreciation for the game.

The silly vibe and 70's-science fiction aesthetic are good, it has the bones of a decent l4d-like but is plagued with just being a real bag of spanners.

Shocking AI, samey enemies, rubbish guns/gunplay, very little episodic content etc 

This could have been great, they just naffed it up. Shame.
Lol with friends.... DIE BLOBS DIE

This is a fun small game with a really nice community. I haven't played much but I've enjoyed all the times I have played, I've met some of the nicest gamers during these events and had some great laughs. This is not a popular game and if you want to play with others then it is highly recommended that you join the Stray Bombay discord group!

The game is far from perfect, but it's small and cheap! There's really very little to complain about! This game does not deserve the negative reviews it has been receiving.

Bland copy and paste environment, Devs don't really care for the community, and it feels like a soulless attempt to copy the Left 4 Dead style of gameplay. The gunplay leaves something to be desired, and the characters just aren't able to grasp the ability to be iconic. The multi-player is disappointing, with very few actual players, with a large amount of the time just not working properly.

I can forgive alot, but what this feels like is just another "Person who worked on L4D/L4D2 is on this project!!!11!!". Just another failure at an attempt to be like L4D rather then their own thing. That is the only reason to bring up L4D, is to try to hype up L4D players into trying a game that fails to do what L4D did. The vibe is off, I can't really connect with these characters as much as I could with the cast of L4D and L4D2.

The game is fun for maybe an hour or two, if you can get into a lobby with your friends, because its really hard to screw up a horde shooter outside of that its easy to quickly lose interest.
